parts:
Thanks Brya for the detailed description of your issue and a breakdown of what you have done.

Error in round(S[j, colid]) :
  non-numeric argument to mathematical function

I tried to follow the advice in response to posts sharing a similar issue, but I was not able to solve it
https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/oXDXmhQ1OOI
https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/zJcUpGNseUg

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sleep log issues
parts:
This may indicate that the M5 L5 (MXLX) calculation is struggling. GGIR should be able to handle various scenarios. To investigate please run GGIR multiple times with each of the settings below and assess when GGIR produces useful output and when not. For this you can set mode = 2 and do.report = 2 as these arguments only affect part 2 and part 2 is where you got the error:
  1. winhr =c(), qwindow = c()
  2. winhr = c(0.5, 1.0), qwindow = c()
  3. winhr = c(0.5, 1.0), qwindow = c(8)
  4. winhr = c(0.5, 1.0), qwindow = c(6, 8)
  5. winhr = c(0.5, 1.0), qwindow = c(6, 8, 15.25, 18.5)
  6. winhr = c(0.16667, 0.5, 1.0), qwindow = c(6, 8, 15.25, 18.5)

I suspect that the problem is that you are using narrow windows, and even though GGIR should be able to handle small windows you may have found an edge case where it does not work.

Please report back as it would be good to know the result.

Cheers, Vincent
Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

parts:
Hi Bryan,

Sorry, I now see that our thread has been idle since December. I have been offline and now catching up.

Your rar file does not include the meta/basic folder content, by which I am not able to reproduce the error. However, I just had another look at your script and see "winhr = c(0.16667, 0.5, 1.0)". This would mean that you ask GGIR to look for the most active consecutive 10 minutes in the day.

If you are trying to replicate the MX metrics by Alex Rowlands and colleagues then please not that you should extract them with the qlevels argument in GGIR, which looks at the percentile corresponding to the most active non-consecutive X minutes or hours in a day.

I know it is very confusing that both methods can be referred to as MX, but there is a big difference in looking for the most active consecutive or non-consecutive minutes.

May I propose that you first try to process your data without specifying arguments winhr and qlevels (set them to c() or delete the config.csv file). Once that generates plausible output, refine your analyse by iteratively adding a new argument and running the analysis to identify whether and when you run into new error. For this new iterations you do not need to specify mode = 1 anymore, because there arguments will only affect part 2 analyses. However, I would recommend not using winhr with values less than 1 any longer as I am not sure there is any theoretical basis for it and because GGIR may not be ready to make sense of it either.

Best, Vincent
